context: Introduce explicit Snowflake stage-path recognition in benchbox/utils/cloud_storage.py rather than widening the scheme list — stage paths are a distinct namespace, not a URI. Add is_snowflake_stage_path() covering the three forms: user stage (@~/...), table stage (@%table/...) and named stage (@stage/... and @db.schema.stage/...). Treat a stage path as NON-local everywhere is_cloud_path currently gates, and give get_cloud_path_info a stage branch that reports a stage provider with the stage name and sub-path instead of falling through to the local shape. In orchestrator._resolve_custom_output_root, route stage paths through CloudStagingPath exactly as s3:// is routed, so datagen lands in the managed local cache under the resolved runs root AND platform_cfg['staging_root'] is populated for the adapter. Mirror the same gate in _resolve_construction_output_dir so the pre-construction path returns None (deferred resolution) rather than the raw string. Add '@~/' to .gitignore as defence in depth. This item deliberately does NOT change what Snowflake does with the stage at load time — it only stops the path from being mistaken for a local directory; adapter-side stage upload is out of scope.
description: benchbox/utils/cloud_storage.py::is_cloud_path classifies purely by URI scheme (urlparse().scheme in s3/gs/gcs/az/abfss/azure/dbfs). Snowflake INTERNAL stage paths carry no scheme, so `@~/benchbox` classifies as local. Verified on 2026-07-24 @ 14b0271c1 by direct probe: is_cloud_path('@~/benchbox') is False and create_path_handler('@~/benchbox') returns PosixPath('@~/benchbox') — a RELATIVE path. The full chain: benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py::_apply_default_cloud_output_dir reads default_output_location from stored Snowflake credentials (the maintainer's is literally '@~/benchbox') into self.custom_output_dir; benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py::_resolve_construction_output_dir returns it verbatim as a LOCAL output_dir because the is_cloud_path gate says False; BaseBenchmark.__init__ passes it to create_path_handler and datagen writes to <cwd>/@~/benchbox/. Observed impact: 319 MB of TPC-H SF1 .tbl.zst plus a _datagen_manifest.json landed in a literal '@~' directory inside the repo checkout on 2026-07-24 at 08:42. Second-order defect on the same gate: benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py::_resolve_custom_output_root early-returns on the not-is_cloud_path branch BEFORE setting platform_cfg['staging_root'], so the Snowflake adapter never learns a stage was configured and silently falls back to internal-stage loading; had staging_root been set, benchbox/platforms/snowflake.py would have logged the nonsense 'local://None' from get_cloud_path_info. The '@~' directory is also not gitignored (benchmark_runs/ is, at .gitignore:68), which is why the 319 MB showed as untracked while the larger in-tree spill did not.

anti_patterns.dont: Add '@~' or a bare '@' to the urlparse scheme list in is_cloud_path
anti_patterns.instead: Match the stage namespace with a dedicated predicate and call it alongside the scheme check
anti_patterns.why: A stage path has no URI scheme at all, so urlparse never produces one; matching on the scheme list cannot express this and would silently misfire on other schemeless input

anti_patterns.dont: Classify any path merely containing '@' as a stage
anti_patterns.instead: Anchor the match to a leading '@' and validate the stage-name grammar that follows
anti_patterns.why: abfss://container@account.dfs.core.windows.net/... contains '@' and is already handled as a cloud URI; a blanket match would reroute Azure paths

anti_patterns.dont: Fix this by editing the stored credential to an s3:// URL
anti_patterns.instead: Fix the classification so any stage path is structurally incapable of becoming a local directory
anti_patterns.why: It hides the defect for one machine while every future user who accepts the credential prompt's advertised @~/benchbox default hits the same 319 MB spill

deferrals.reason: Re-wrapping a CloudStagingPath downgrades it to a plain local Path, dropping cloud_target. Verified identical for s3:// and stage (both return PosixPath('/tmp/cache')), so this is pre-existing behaviour, NOT a regression from this item, and the orchestrator carries the remote target via platform_cfg['staging_root'] instead. Adding the pass-through would change s3:// handler types, which this item's must-preserve list forbids ('s3:// ... continue to classify exactly as today'). Needs its own item covering all CloudStagingPath producers.
deferrals.summary: create_path_handler has no CloudStagingPath pass-through, unlike the DatabricksPath 'avoids double-wrapping' guard

preserves.behavior: An explicit --output on the command line keeps priority over the credential-derived default
Genuine local paths — absolute, relative, and ~-prefixed — continue to classify as local
Snowflake's existing internal-stage load path is unchanged; this item only fixes path classification, not adapter upload behaviour
cloudpathlib stays lazily imported and is not required for stage paths
s3://, gs://, gcs://, az://, abfss://, azure:// and dbfs:/Volumes/ continue to classify exactly as today, including the DatabricksPath temp-dir behaviour

prior_art.concept: _resolve_custom_output_root already branches cloud vs local and sets platform_cfg['staging_root']
CloudStagingPath / DatabricksPath — persistent local cache plus remote target, the established wrapper for 'generate locally, upload later'
is_databricks_path() — an existing non-cloudpathlib special case bolted onto the same classification gate

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/utils/ -k 'cloud or path or stage' -q
verifications.description: Cloud-storage path classification unit tests pass, including the new stage cases

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from pathlib import Path; from benchbox.utils.cloud_storage import is_cloud_path, create_path_handler; p='@~/benchbox'; assert is_cloud_path(p), 'stage still classified local'; h=create_path_handler(p); assert not (isinstance(h, Path) and not h.is_absolute()), h; print('ok', h)"
verifications.description: A stage path no longer resolves to a relative local directory
verifications.expected: prints ok with a non-relative handler, exit 0

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/cli/ -k 'output_root or staging' -q
verifications.description: Orchestrator routes a stage path to a local cache and sets staging_root

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "import tempfile, os, pathlib; from benchbox.utils.cloud_storage import create_path_handler; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); os.chdir(d); h=create_path_handler('@~/benchbox'); stray=pathlib.Path(d)/'@~'; assert not stray.exists(), stray; assert not (isinstance(h, pathlib.Path) and not h.is_absolute()), h; print('ok', h)"
verifications.description: Resolving a stage path from a clean temp cwd creates no stray directory
verifications.expected: prints ok with a non-relative handler and no @~ directory created, exit 0

work_units.evidence: Added is_snowflake_stage_path() to benchbox/utils/cloud_storage.py with an anchored regex (_SNOWFLAKE_STAGE_RE) covering user (@~), table (@%tbl), named (@stage) and qualified (@db.schema.stage) forms, incl. double-quoted identifiers. work_units.evidence: is_cloud_path() now returns True for stage paths via the dedicated predicate (scheme list untouched, per anti-pattern). get_cloud_path_info() gained a snowflake_stage branch reporting provider=snowflake_stage, bucket=<stage>, path=<sub-path> and stage_info={stage,sub_path}, mirroring the existing dbfs volume_info precedent. create_path_handler() gained a stage branch returning CloudStagingPath(mkdtemp, stage) BEFORE the cloudpathlib fallthrough, so cloudpathlib stays lazy and no relative Path is ever returned.
work_units.notes: This is what stops benchbox/platforms/snowflake.py logging the nonsense 'local://None' when staging_root is a stage path.
work_units.summary: Make is_cloud_path treat stage paths as non-local, and give get_cloud_path_info a stage branch reporting a snowflake_stage provider with stage name and sub-path
